rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4 - the authors process 8 PlanetScope SR images of the Araguaia River (Jan-Jul 2018), extract water areas by NDVI threshold and regress them against gauge and altimetry data (Tables 1-2, Fig. 5). Q2: Section 4, Eqs. 2-4, Fig. 5, Table 3 - CubeSat flood area in the 500 m buffer explains river flow (R2 96.49%), water level (R2 94.38%) and altimetry (R2 88.83%); Discussion states CubeSat flood areas gave a higher correlation with the gauge than the JASON-2 virtual station used by ANA. Q3: Sections 3.2 and 5 - the CubeSat-derived estimate is checked against two independent references, the in-situ conventional gauge (flow and level) and JASON-2 satellite altimetry (Fig. 4b, Fig. 5). Q4: Section 4, Fig. 4a and Table 2 - the study measures the intermediate chain: gauge level-flow rating (R2=1), flooded water-body area per buffer from NDVI, and area-level-flow regressions. Q7: Sections 4-5 - a buffer of at least 500 m (0.5-1 times the mean river width) was the smallest giving a high and stable R2; usable images must be cloud-free, fully cover the buffer and be surface-reflectance products (Table 1). Q8: Section 5 - only 8 image dates were usable (cloud/incomplete/TOA), proof-of-concept on one river predicting at monthly scale, lower accuracy at high discharge when level rises inside the channel without expanding flooded area, CubeSats lack MIR/SWIR bands so only NDVI could be used. Q9: Table 3 - standard deviation of residuals reported as precision estimator for estimated flow (553.63 m3/s), level (37.16 cm) and altimetry (0.34 m); ranges of water-body areas given in Section 4.
rows.notes: Study directly demonstrates CubeSat-based river flow and water-level estimation on one station of the Araguaia River. The passage's downstream implication (sub-basin discharge monitoring for efficient water management in developing countries) is stated by the authors only as a potential application/recommendation and is not tested; I treated the core claim (accurate river flow and height estimation from CubeSats) as the rated effect. Q6 no: single cross-section/virtual station, sub-basin and continental monitoring are future-work statements. Q5 no: single river, single site, one season. Q9 is borderline: the SD reported is the dispersion of estimation residuals (precision), alongside RMSE which alone would not count.

notes: Full text available and complete. The claim's water-management/conservation benefit is only asserted by the study, not evidenced; the rating reflects the river-flow estimation result which is the substantive content of the passage.
